title: Tritium self-sufficiency through breeding blankets
bottleneck: Tritium has a 12.3-year half-life and essentially no natural supply: a 1 GW fusion plant would burn roughly 56 kg per year while the world holds only about 25 kg commercially. Every D-T plant must therefore breed its own tritium by capturing fusion neutrons in lithium-bearing blankets, achieving a tritium breeding ratio above 1.1 to cover losses and build startup inventory. No blanket design has yet demonstrated net tritium breeding in a burning-plasma environment.
why_it_blocks: Without proven self-sufficient breeding, the entire D-T fusion fuel cycle collapses. There is no external tritium market that could fuel more than one or two plants, so breeding is a gating requirement, not an optimization.
current_state: Blanket concepts such as helium-cooled pebble bed and water-cooled lithium-lead are being tested in non-nuclear mockups and ITER test blanket modules. Integrated breeding at power-plant scale remains unproven.
